searchText: Would be really helpful if there was. All closed source websites show a different supply. I don't want to feed bitcoiners 😛 naively the CL side is easy, you can get `/validators/balances` and sum them I think Peter from Geth worked on something for the EL side? Would be cool if there was one endpoint that would return a breakdown as seen here <https://etherscan.io/stat/supply> if there is one endpoint all explorers use, then i am sure the supply will be the same everywhere and lead to less confusion <https://etherscan.io/stat/supply> > 120,521,607.46 > Total Ether Supply <https://ultrasound.money/> > CURRENT SUPPLY > 120,522,316 <https://messari.io/asset/ethereum/metrics/all> > Circulating Supply > 122,373,863.50 not a good look imho <:thonkSweat:977085374432153640> yeah fair, I think it would need to be two endpoints, one CL and one EL The calculator could also be a side-car, does not necessarily need to be integrated into the clients we published this for CL <https://github.com/gobitfly/eth-rewards> which will be used for: this is awesome, I saw! we've also got an Ethereum protocol fellow interested in speccing some standard APIs to make this data easier to get at (<https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/issues/3661>) For the Merge Data Challenge, I analyzed on-chain attestation data: https://twitter.com/AnotherJannik/status/1585596638478966784 No mind-blowing insights, but maybe a few bits and pieces that could interesting to some. For instance that the "disagreement" among attestations increased by a factor of 10 at the merge (but is still very small). <@97774605351010304> I have not used this feature yet, but maybe erigons `--watch-the-burn Enable WatchTheBurn stage to keep track of ETH issuance` helps? I think they have an API function for that, too

excerpts.author: jannik031153
excerpts.content:
For the Merge Data Challenge, I analyzed on-chain attestation data: https://twitter.com/AnotherJannik/status/1585596638478966784

No mind-blowing insights, but maybe a few bits and pieces that could interesting to some. For instance that the "disagreement" among attestations increased by a factor of 10 at the merge (but is still very small).
